thread: How the sickness first gets into the body

evidence.clue: Ch2-3: Jaina does not know whether it enters through food, water or air; the doe could have drunk, eaten or lain in it; horses are clean.
Chapter 4: in every newly ill person it is only under the breastbone and along the gut; in the late case it radiates outward from the gut. So it is swallowed.

Chapter 4: water does not sort them (three houses on the Cooper's Lane well run worst to best); contact does not (Garran lives alone and is worst); grain in general does not (Col ate oats all summer). What sorts them is bread from one flour: Garran (sops morning and night for months), the cooper's house (two loaves a day), Col (two nights of bread), Wenna (store flour since harvest, the heel of each loaf), Elsie (two pieces at noon). Mother Haw (own oats, same well) is well.
Chapter 4: confirmed by stopping the bread: by dawn Elsie's fever breaks, the cooper's boy and Col are well, Wenna is sleeping, only the late case holds.

readerKnows: The sickness is swallowed in flour (bread), one supplier, cumulative with dose.
povCharacterKnows: Jaina and Sylvanas know; Brask and Tobin know; the party knows the flour is deliberately sold.
notes: Resolved as to entry. Open: how the contamination also reached Millhaven's well, the doe and the ground (water carries a little); what turns the sick into walking dead; whether the dose is lethal in all cases.
